newsitem.title: CANADA: Pools to return tendered UGG shares, retain theirs.
newsitem.headline: Pools to return tendered UGG shares, retain theirs.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool chief financial officer said about 854,000 limited common voting shares in United Grain Growers Ltd will be returned to Lindner Growth Fund and individual investors.
"Shares that were tendered to Montreal Trust and our elevators will be returned," AWP chief financial officer Geoff Southwood told reporters on a conference call.

About 54,000 individuals, many farmers, tendered their UGG shares to AWP and co-bidder Manitoba Pool Elevators after they announced their C$172 million hostile takeover bid Feb 20 when it unveiled a lock-up agreement for Lindner's shares.

AWP and MPE made a C$172 million hostile takeover bid for UGG on February 20 after announcing a lock-up agreement with U.S. mutual fund Lindner Growth Fund for their 800,000 shares, or 6.4 percent of UGG stock, in addition to the 14.98 percent they already owned.
"We will retain our shares in UGG," Southwood said. "We don't plan to appeal the decision."
UGG's board of directors had adopted a shareholder rights plan earlier any shareholder, other than a hostile bidder, the option to purchase 8.5 more shares for each one already held at C$5.88 each.
Manitoba Judge John Scollin ruled earlier Tuesday that the Pools' irrevocable lock-up with Lindner had triggered the poison pill.
UGG's board will meet shortly to consider setting the separation time for the rights issued under the plan, after which the rights will be exercisable.

Southwood estimated the Pools' C$21 million investment in acquiring 14.98 percent of UGG stock could be diluted to two percent if all other UGG shareholders are granted and exercise the option to purchase 8.5 more shares at C$5.88 for each share they already own.
